title: When God Revealed His Gracious Name
description: When God Revealed His Gracious Name in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 642 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Experience of God's Grace”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: When God re-vealed his gra-cious name, And changed my mourn-ful state, My rap-ture seemed a pleas-ing dream, The grace ap-peared so great.

lines: When God revealed his gracious name,
My rapture seemed a pleasing dream,
The world beheld the glorious change,
My tongue broke out in unknown strains,
The Lord can clear the darkest skies,
Can give us day for night;
Make drops of sacred sorrow rise
Let those, who sow in sadness, wait
They shall confess their sheaves are great,

licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
